diagnosis.question: which term carries the 340 m
diagnosis.evidence: The host's tick_state was an empty override at both binding sites (src/game_hosts_units.cpp), so through 664 live aimdive ticks of local/usn04_pitchgate.log and local/usn04_d4h.log the dive-bomb task issued no roll and no pitch. With no task command the pitch mode stayed at the 2 the reset leaves and the planner's own pitch arm levelled the aircraft, which flew past the target.
diagnosis.arithmetic: The aim error model is consistent with the census and is NOT the fault. At the closest sample - |error| 359.50 m, range 444.2 m, altitude 631.2 m - the model gives x0 = 350 + 100 = 450, x1 = 1000 + 0 = 1000, t = (631.2 - 450) / 550 = 0.3295, lead = 23.06, gain = 0.7694. Solving gain * (cos(bearing) * 444.2 - 23.06) = -359.50 gives cos(bearing) = -0.99998, i.e. the target dead astern. The positive branch would need cos(bearing) = 1.104 and is impossible. So the closest the error ever came to the window was with the aircraft already past the target at 444 m of miss distance.
diagnosis.ruled_out: Not a wrong input: the lead's first suspect, approach->vtable[0], resolves to 009C40A0, which returns the approach's own aim point, and the host's bearing and planar distance are drawn from the commanded target the same way (009C7B4F-009C7BB0 against the host's block at src/game_hosts_units.cpp). Not a unit error: every term is in metres and radians on both sides.

corrections.was: approach+50h is an extra range with no producer read, carried as db_extra_range_50 and substituted at 0.0
corrections.is: it is component 1 - the vertical component - of the approach's aim point, which approach->vtable[0] at 009C40A0 hands out
corrections.evidence: The vtable 00D20C48 the constructor writes at 009C3EE2 has 009C40A0 in slot 0, and 009C40A0 copies [ECX+4Ch], [ECX+50h] and [ECX+54h] to out[0], out[1] and out[2]. The aimdive tick then takes out[0] and out[2] as the horizontal pair for its atan2 and its planar distance, and subtracts out[1] from the aircraft's Y to get the height above the aim point - so +50h is a height. That also makes the aim error's x1 = approach+ACh + approach+50h coherent, altitude plus altitude. 009C8D40 writes all three offsets (009C8D9B, 009C8F27, 009C8F2E) with ESI = ECX = the approach from 009C8D45, but whether it is the only writer is NOT established. The 0.0 substitution stays numerically right for a sea-level target; the name db_extra_range_50 is what is wrong.
